disclaimer: Synthetic Saudi retail demonstration model and data. Not an ANB model, not an ANB policy, not a SAMA requirement, and not independently validated. No credit decision should rest on it.
purpose: To identify retail customers whose position is deteriorating before it reaches arrears, and to separate those who are already in trouble from those who are still paying and are likely to deteriorate.
target: Deterioration in the customer's credit position over the next reporting months, evidenced by governed triggers rather than by a fitted probability. The score ranks and explains; it does not claim a calibrated default probability.
horizon: One to three reporting months. Every trigger is evaluated at a month-end against that month's book and the months behind it.
eligible_population: Every open retail facility in the published book at the scoring month, and every customer holding one.

scale.direction: Higher is worse. 0 is a customer with nothing firing.

threshold_source: Synthetic demo threshold — bank-configurable, not an ANB or regulatory limit

action_dimensions.name: Direction
action_dimensions.meaning: Whether the underlying measure is improving, stable or deteriorating.
action_dimensions.computed: The sign of this month's value against last month's, on the trigger's own direction of risk. A measure where lower is worse deteriorates when it falls.

action_dimensions.name: Magnitude
action_dimensions.meaning: How big this month's move is, relative to the trigger's threshold.
action_dimensions.computed: The absolute one-month change over the trigger's threshold, capped at 3. A move of exactly the threshold is 1.0.

action_dimensions.name: Velocity
action_dimensions.meaning: How fast the measure is moving.
action_dimensions.computed: The mean monthly change over the last three months, in the measure's own unit.
action_dimensions.values: Signed, in the variable's unit per month

action_dimensions.name: Momentum
action_dimensions.meaning: Whether the deterioration is accelerating or slowing.
action_dimensions.computed: This month's change less the mean change of the two months before it. Positive on a worsening measure means it is getting worse faster.

action_dimensions.name: Persistence
action_dimensions.meaning: How long the trigger has been firing without a break.
action_dimensions.computed: Consecutive months the trigger has fired, counting back from this month.

action_dimensions.name: Recency
action_dimensions.meaning: How recently the relevant observation was made.
action_dimensions.computed: Months since the observation the trigger reads. Zero for a measure refreshed with this month's book; for bureau it is months since the last dated pull.

hard_triggers.name: A high-severity trigger fired
hard_triggers.condition: any trigger of severity HIGH fired
hard_triggers.because: The Bureau and Facility layers carry fifteen per cent each, so a lone trigger inside either one cannot arithmetically reach the warning cutoff however serious it is. A new external delinquency scored thirteen and never appeared on a warning list. A high-severity trigger means the customer is to be looked at, and the score has to say so.

hard_triggers.name: A critical trigger fired
hard_triggers.condition: any trigger of severity CRITICAL fired
hard_triggers.because: Same arithmetic, one band higher: a critical observation in a lightly weighted layer is still a critical observation.

hard_triggers.name: Ninety or more days past due
hard_triggers.because: At ninety days the deterioration has already happened. No combination of quiet layers should be able to report it as anything but critical.

hard_triggers.name: IFRS 9 Stage 3
hard_triggers.because: Credit-impaired under the bank's own impairment policy.

hard_triggers.name: Entered default this month
hard_triggers.because: The event the whole system exists to anticipate has occurred; the score must not read below it.

hard_triggers.name: Forbearance with arrears
hard_triggers.because: A concession was granted and the customer fell behind anyway, which is the clearest evidence a restructure has not worked.

layers.name: Behavioural Intelligence
layers.weight_because: Weighted highest because its triggers are the least ambiguous evidence in the book: the customer either paid or did not.

sublayers.name: Delinquency
sublayers.purpose: Where the arrears are now and which way they are going.

triggers.name: Delinquency bucket worsening
triggers.meaning: Days past due rose materially in one month and the facility is now thirty days down or worse.
triggers.reason_template: Days past due rose from {comparator:.0f} to {value:.0f} in one month.
triggers.recommended_review: Confirm the arrears position and the collections action already taken.

triggers.name: Early-life payment failure
triggers.meaning: A payment was missed within the first six months on book, which says the underwriting was wrong rather than that circumstances changed.
triggers.reason_template: A payment was missed within the first six months on book ({comparator:.0f} months on book, {value:.0f} missed).
triggers.recommended_review: Check the origination file: affordability evidence, income verification and any exception.

triggers.name: Delinquency recurrence
triggers.meaning: The facility has been thirty days down inside six months and is current again: a cure that may not hold.
triggers.reason_template: Reached {value:.0f} days past due within six months and is current again.
triggers.recommended_review: Check whether the cure was a payment or a concession.

classifiers.name: Delinquency bucket
classifiers.meaning: The customer's arrears band at this month-end, as the book publishes it.

classifiers.name: Months on book
classifiers.meaning: Whole months since origination. An early-life failure is read differently from a failure in year four.

classifiers.name: Origination vintage
classifiers.meaning: The cohort the facility was written in.

sublayers.name: Payment Performance
sublayers.purpose: Whether the scheduled payment is arriving at all.

triggers.name: Consecutive missed payments
triggers.meaning: Two or more scheduled payments missed in three months.
triggers.reason_template: {value:.0f} scheduled payments missed in the last three months.
triggers.recommended_review: Review affordability and whether a restructure is warranted.

triggers.name: Broken promises to pay
triggers.meaning: Promises made to collections and not kept. The customer engaged and still did not pay.
triggers.reason_template: {value:.0f} promises to pay were not honoured in three months.
triggers.recommended_review: Escalate the collections approach; repeated broken promises rarely self-correct.

triggers.name: Repeated direct-debit failure
triggers.meaning: Automatic payment attempts returned unpaid, which usually means the account is empty on the due date.
triggers.reason_template: {value:.0f} direct-debit attempts were returned in three months.
triggers.recommended_review: Check the funding account and the salary credit date against the instalment date.

triggers.name: Returned payments
triggers.meaning: Payments presented and returned unpaid.
triggers.reason_template: {value:.0f} payments were returned unpaid in three months.
triggers.recommended_review: Check the funding arrangement.

triggers.name: Partial payments
triggers.meaning: Instalments part-paid rather than missed.
triggers.reason_template: {value:.0f} instalments part-paid in three months.
triggers.recommended_review: Review affordability.
triggers.absent_because: The published book records missed and returned payments but not part-payments, so this trigger is declared and never evaluated rather than approximated from another column.

classifiers.name: Payment to amount due
classifiers.meaning: What share of the amount due was actually paid this month. One is paid in full; a part-payment is read differently from a miss.

classifiers.name: Months paid in full
classifiers.meaning: How many of the last six months were settled in full. The baseline a missed payment is read against.

sublayers.name: Utilisation and Usage
sublayers.purpose: How hard a revolving facility is being used, and on what.

triggers.name: Persistent minimum payment
triggers.meaning: Only the contractual minimum paid, every month, for three months.
triggers.reason_template: Only the minimum payment was made in {value:.0f} of the last three months.
triggers.recommended_review: Review the customer's wider affordability.

triggers.name: Rising card utilisation
triggers.meaning: Utilisation climbed sharply over three months.
triggers.reason_template: Utilisation rose {value:.0f} percentage points over three months.
triggers.recommended_review: Check what the balance was spent on and whether the limit is still appropriate.

triggers.name: Over-limit activity
triggers.meaning: Days spent above the credit limit.
triggers.reason_template: {value:.0f} day(s) above the credit limit in three months.
triggers.recommended_review: Confirm the limit and the excess authorisation.

triggers.name: Rising cash advances
triggers.meaning: Cash advance is expensive money taken by somebody who has run out of cheaper money.
triggers.reason_template: Cash advances were {value:.0%} of card spend over three months.
triggers.recommended_review: Review the customer's liquidity.

classifiers.name: Card behaviour segment
classifiers.meaning: Transactor, revolver or inactive. A revolver at eighty per cent utilisation is normal; a transactor at eighty per cent is not.

classifiers.name: Utilisation band
classifiers.meaning: The facility's drawn share of its limit, banded.

classifiers.name: Revolving or amortising
classifiers.meaning: Whether the facility revolves. An amortising loan has no utilisation and this sublayer scores zero for it.

sublayers.name: Behavioural Score Dynamics
sublayers.purpose: What the bank's own behavioural scorecard is saying.

triggers.name: Behavioural score deterioration
triggers.meaning: The bank's own behavioural score fell materially in one month.
triggers.reason_template: Behavioural score fell from {comparator:.0f} to {value:.0f}.
triggers.recommended_review: Read the scorecard's own reason codes beside this.

triggers.name: Score-band migration
triggers.meaning: The customer moved down a behavioural grade.
triggers.reason_template: Behavioural grade moved down from {comparator} to {value}.
triggers.recommended_review: Check which inputs moved the grade.

classifiers.name: Behavioural score band
classifiers.meaning: The customer's behavioural grade this month.

classifiers.name: Application score band
classifiers.meaning: What the customer scored at origination. The baseline a behavioural move is read against.

layers.name: Affordability & Cash Flow Intelligence
layers.weight_because: Weighted second because it is the earliest honest evidence in the book: a salary that stops arriving precedes a missed instalment by a month or two.

sublayers.name: Income Stability
sublayers.purpose: Whether verified income is holding up.

triggers.name: Material income decline
triggers.meaning: The latest salary credit is materially below the average of the three before it.
triggers.reason_template: The latest salary credit is {value:.0%} of the recent average.
triggers.recommended_review: Confirm the income position before any further lending.

triggers.name: Salary volatility
triggers.meaning: Salary credits swinging month to month.
triggers.reason_template: Salary credits vary by {value:.0%} around their six-month mean.
triggers.recommended_review: Check whether income is variable by arrangement or by disruption.

classifiers.name: Employment status
classifiers.meaning: Salaried, self-employed or otherwise. The shape of an income interruption differs between them.

classifiers.name: Employer sector
classifiers.meaning: Where the customer works. Not their industry as a borrower.

classifiers.name: Verified income
classifiers.meaning: Verified monthly salary plus verified other income. A customer property, counted once.

sublayers.name: Salary Behaviour
sublayers.purpose: Whether the salary is arriving at all.

triggers.name: Salary credit interruption
triggers.meaning: A salary cycle passed with no credit at all.
triggers.reason_template: {value:.0f} salary cycles with no credit in the last three months.
triggers.recommended_review: Confirm employment before the next instalment falls due.

triggers.name: Consecutive salary-missing months
triggers.meaning: Two or more consecutive cycles with no salary credit. Employment has probably ended.
triggers.reason_template: {value:.0f} consecutive salary cycles with no credit.
triggers.recommended_review: Treat as an employment event, not a payment event.

classifiers.name: Salary transfer
classifiers.meaning: Whether salary is mandated to this bank. Without it the absence of a credit says nothing.

classifiers.name: Expected credit date
classifiers.meaning: When the salary is due, so a late credit can be told from an absent one.

sublayers.name: Debt Burden
sublayers.purpose: What share of income the customer's obligations take.

triggers.name: Affordability deterioration
triggers.meaning: The share of income taken by credit obligations rose materially in one month.
triggers.reason_template: Debt burden rose from {comparator:.0%} to {value:.0%}.
triggers.recommended_review: Identify the new obligation and whether it was disclosed.

triggers.name: New external obligations
triggers.meaning: Monthly obligations to other lenders rose. The customer is borrowing elsewhere.
triggers.reason_template: Monthly obligations to other lenders rose by SAR {value:,.0f} over three months.
triggers.recommended_review: Review the customer's total indebtedness.

classifiers.name: Debt burden at origination
classifiers.meaning: The ratio the facility was underwritten at. The baseline a movement is read against.

sublayers.name: Disposable Income and Affordability
sublayers.purpose: What is left after everything is paid.

triggers.name: Disposable income decline
triggers.meaning: Income less household expenses less obligations fell materially.
triggers.reason_template: Disposable income fell by SAR {magnitude:,.0f} in one month.
triggers.recommended_review: Check which side of the calculation moved.

classifiers.name: Indebtedness band
classifiers.meaning: Where the customer's debt burden sits, banded.

sublayers.name: Cash-Flow Stress
sublayers.purpose: Whether there is money in the account when it is needed.

triggers.name: Personal cash buffer exhausted
triggers.meaning: The average account balance no longer covers half a monthly instalment.
triggers.reason_template: Average balance covers {value:.1f} months of the instalment.
triggers.recommended_review: Check the salary credit date against the instalment date.

triggers.name: Account inflow decline
triggers.meaning: Money arriving in the account fell against its own recent average.
triggers.reason_template: Account inflows fell SAR {magnitude:,.0f} below their three-month average.
triggers.recommended_review: Read beside the salary triggers: an inflow fall with salary intact is a different story.

layers.name: Bureau & External Credit Intelligence
layers.weight_because: Weighted lowest of the four because most months carry no new bureau observation at all. A layer that cannot move most of the time must not be able to move the overall score much when it does.
layers.refresh: On a dated pull only: at origination, on the customer's own re-pull cadence, and on entry to thirty days past due. Never monthly.

sublayers.name: Bureau Risk Profile
sublayers.purpose: Where the customer sits with the bureau, as last seen.

triggers.name: Bureau deterioration
triggers.meaning: The bureau score fell between two DATED pulls. It cannot fire in a month with no new observation.
triggers.reason_template: Bureau score fell from {comparator:.0f} to {value:.0f} between observations.
triggers.recommended_review: Check what the bureau saw that this bank has not.

classifiers.name: Last observed bureau score
classifiers.meaning: The bureau score at the last dated pull, carried forward unchanged until the next one.

classifiers.name: Bureau score at origination
classifiers.meaning: What the bureau said when the facility was written.

classifiers.name: Bureau risk band
classifiers.meaning: The last observed score, banded.

sublayers.name: External Delinquency
sublayers.purpose: Whether the customer is behind with somebody else.

triggers.name: New external delinquency
triggers.meaning: A new arrears position with another lender, observed at a dated pull.
triggers.reason_template: External arrears rose from {comparator:.0f} to {value:.0f} days at the latest bureau observation.
triggers.recommended_review: A customer paying this bank and not another is choosing; find out why.

classifiers.name: Worst external days past due
classifiers.meaning: The worst arrears with any other lender at the last pull.

sublayers.name: External Leverage
sublayers.purpose: How much the customer owes elsewhere.

triggers.name: External leverage increase
triggers.meaning: Total borrowing elsewhere rose between pulls.
triggers.reason_template: Bureau exposure rose SAR {magnitude:,.0f} between observations.
triggers.recommended_review: Reassess total indebtedness.

classifiers.name: External monthly obligations
classifiers.meaning: Monthly obligations to other lenders at the last pull.

classifiers.name: Total bureau exposure
classifiers.meaning: Everything the bureau shows outstanding.

sublayers.name: Credit Seeking and Enquiries
sublayers.purpose: Whether the customer is shopping for credit.

triggers.name: New credit enquiries
triggers.meaning: More searches than at the last pull. Somebody looking hard for credit is often about to need it.
triggers.reason_template: {value:.0f} bureau enquiries at the latest observation, against {comparator:.0f} before.
triggers.recommended_review: Read beside the affordability layer.

classifiers.name: Bureau enquiries
classifiers.meaning: Searches recorded against the customer at the last pull.

sublayers.name: Data Recency
sublayers.purpose: How old the external picture is. The one sublayer here that moves every month, because staleness accrues whether or not anything else happens.

triggers.name: Bureau information is stale
triggers.meaning: A year or more since the last dated bureau observation. Not a statement about the customer; a statement about what is known about them.
triggers.reason_template: The bureau position is {value:.0f} months old.
triggers.recommended_review: Order a refreshed bureau report before acting on the external layer.

classifiers.name: Last bureau observation date
classifiers.meaning: The month-end of the last dated bureau pull.

layers.name: Facility & Exposure Intelligence
layers.weight_because: Weighted lowest of the three dynamic layers because a structural signal describes the contract rather than the customer, and is strongest when read beside the other three.

sublayers.name: Exposure Build-up
sublayers.purpose: Whether what is owed is growing.

triggers.name: Rapid balance build
triggers.meaning: Outstanding balance grew more than a fifth in one month on an amortising facility, which should be shrinking. Revolving facilities are out of scope: a card balance that grows is a card being used.
triggers.reason_template: Balance rose {value:.0%} in one month.
triggers.recommended_review: Identify the draw or the top-up behind it.
triggers.absent_because: Not observable in this book. A top-up here is written as a NEW facility rather than added to an existing one, so an amortising balance never grows: the largest one-month rise across twenty months is one per cent, which is interest accrual. The trigger is declared and never evaluated rather than having its threshold lowered until ordinary accrual reads as a warning.

classifiers.name: Amount financed
classifiers.meaning: What was lent at origination.

classifiers.name: Contract structure
classifiers.meaning: How the facility repays. A balance that grows on an amortising contract is a different event from one that grows on a revolving line.

sublayers.name: Limit and Utilisation
sublayers.purpose: Whether the facility is pressed against its own limit.

triggers.name: Limit excess
triggers.meaning: Drawn balance above the sanctioned limit.
triggers.reason_template: Drawn balance is {value:.0%} of the limit.
triggers.recommended_review: Confirm the excess was authorised.

classifiers.name: Current credit limit
classifiers.meaning: The limit in force at this month-end.

classifiers.name: Original credit limit
classifiers.meaning: The limit sanctioned at origination.

sublayers.name: Restructure and Forbearance
sublayers.purpose: Whether a concession has already been granted.

triggers.name: Forbearance under strain
triggers.meaning: A concession was granted and the customer fell behind anyway.
triggers.reason_template: Forborne and {value:.0f} days past due.
triggers.recommended_review: The restructure has not worked; review the arrangement rather than extending it.

triggers.name: Repeated restructure
triggers.meaning: The contract has been rewritten more than once.
triggers.reason_template: The facility has been restructured {value:.0f} times.
triggers.recommended_review: Repeated restructuring usually defers a loss rather than preventing one.
triggers.absent_because: The published book carries a restructure date and flag but not a lifetime count, so this trigger is declared and never evaluated rather than inferred from a single date.

classifiers.name: Forbearance flag
classifiers.meaning: Whether a concession has been granted because of financial difficulty.

classifiers.name: Restructured flag
classifiers.meaning: Whether the contract has been rewritten.

sublayers.name: Collateral and Coverage
sublayers.purpose: Whether the security still covers the debt.

triggers.name: Collateral cover deterioration
triggers.meaning: Loan-to-value is forty points or more above where the facility was written: the balance has not fallen away from the collateral's value as the schedule intended, or the collateral is worth less than it was.
triggers.reason_template: Loan-to-value is {value:.0%} against {comparator:.0%} at origination.
triggers.recommended_review: Confirm the valuation date before relying on the security.

classifiers.name: Secured or unsecured
classifiers.meaning: Whether anything stands behind the facility.

classifiers.name: Collateral type
classifiers.meaning: What the security is.

classifiers.name: LTV at origination
classifiers.meaning: Amount financed over collateral value when the facility was written.

sublayers.name: Maturity and Balloon Risk
sublayers.purpose: Whether a large instalment is about to fall due.

triggers.name: Balloon payment approaching
triggers.meaning: A balloon instalment falls due within six months and the customer's buffer is thin.
triggers.reason_template: A balloon payment falls due in {value:.0f} months.
triggers.recommended_review: Agree the refinancing or the settlement now, not in month five.

classifiers.name: Balloon band
classifiers.meaning: How large the final instalment is against the rest.

classifiers.name: Remaining tenor
classifiers.meaning: Months left to contractual maturity.

product_emphasis.CREDIT_CARD: Behavioural and facility/utilisation weighted strongest: a card reports distress through how it is used long before an instalment is missed.
product_emphasis.PERSONAL_LOAN: Behavioural and affordability weighted strongest: an unsecured instalment loan fails when income does.
product_emphasis.AUTO_LOAN: Behavioural, affordability and facility/collateral all carry weight: the asset depreciates faster than the balance amortises early in the term.
product_emphasis.HOME_LOAN: Affordability weighted strongest, then behavioural and facility/collateral: a mortgage is a twenty-year affordability position.

sub_products.label: Infinite Card
sub_products.meaning: The top card tier, held by private and affluent customers on the largest limits.
sub_products.derivation: customer_segment in (PRIVATE, AFFLUENT) and current credit limit >= SAR 60,000

sub_products.label: Signature Card
sub_products.derivation: customer_segment in (PRIVATE, AFFLUENT), or MASS_AFFLUENT on a limit >= SAR 50,000

sub_products.label: Platinum Card
sub_products.derivation: customer_segment == MASS_AFFLUENT, or MASS on a limit >= SAR 25,000

sub_products.label: Classic Card
sub_products.meaning: The mass tier, and the largest card population.
sub_products.derivation: everything else on the card book

sub_products.label: Standard Personal Finance
sub_products.meaning: Personal finance written as new money.

sub_products.label: Top-Up Personal Finance
sub_products.meaning: An existing customer borrowing more on an existing facility.

sub_products.label: Buyout Personal Finance
sub_products.meaning: A balance taken over from another lender.

sub_products.label: Used Vehicle Finance
sub_products.meaning: A used vehicle, which depreciates on a different curve.

sub_products.label: Buyout / Refinance Home Finance
sub_products.meaning: A mortgage taken over from another lender.

classifications.label: Salaried
classifications.meaning: Employed, with a monthly salary from an employer.

classifications.label: Non-Salaried
classifications.meaning: Income that does not arrive as an employer's payroll: self-employed and retired customers.

bureau_rule.statement: The bank does not receive a bureau file every month. A bureau observation exists at origination, on the customer's own re-pull cadence, and on entry to thirty days past due. Between observations the last observed values are carried forward unchanged, with the observation date and its age shown beside them. No monthly bureau movement is generated, and the bureau triggers cannot fire in a month that holds no new observation.
bureau_rule.proxy_label: Synthetic bureau proxy — not a live bureau feed.
bureau_rule.no_agreement: There is no live bureau connection and no bureau agreement behind these values. They are generated with the rest of the demonstration book.

bureau_recency.basis: Demonstration parameters, bank-configurable. Not an observed decay rate for any bureau and not a validated model assumption.

glossary.meaning: Early Warning Score. In this deployment it means the model configured in backend/retail/ews_model.py: four layers, eighteen sublayers, and the triggers under them.
Stable context that sets how a trigger should be read. A classifier never fires on its own.
A live deterioration event measured against this month's book and the months behind it.
Whether the measure behind a trigger is improving, stable or deteriorating.
How large this month's move is against the trigger's own threshold.
The mean monthly change over the last three months.
Whether the deterioration is accelerating or slowing.
Consecutive months a trigger has fired.
Months since the observation the trigger reads. Zero for anything refreshed with the monthly book; for bureau it is months since the last dated pull.
Days past due — how many days the oldest unpaid amount on the facility has been outstanding.
Observed default rate. A PORTFOLIO measure: facilities entering default in the month over facilities eligible to at its start. It is never a property of one customer.
Debt burden ratio — monthly credit obligations over verified monthly income.
Significant Increase in Credit Risk — the IFRS 9 test that moves a facility from Stage 1 to Stage 2.
Loan to value — balance over the collateral's value.
IFRS 9 impairment stages: performing, significant increase in credit risk, and credit-impaired.
A customer who is ALREADY in trouble at this month-end: thirty or more days past due, flagged in default, or in Stage 3. Not a prediction.
A customer who is NOT currently bad and whose Early Warning Score is in the HIGH or CRITICAL band. A prediction about somebody who is still paying.

summary.verdict: The reference model cannot be imported as scoring on this release. Of its distinct classifier / trigger inputs, the majority (58) have no canonical field at all, and several of the rest differ in window, unit or definition. Importing its weights or thresholds would produce a score over fields that do not exist.
